title: Lab 02a - Manage Subscriptions and RBAC
summary: In this lab, you learn about role-based access control. You learn how to use permissions and scopes to control what actions identities can and cannot perform. You also learn how to make subscription management easier using management groups.

title: Lab 02b - Manage Governance via Azure Policy
summary: In this lab, you learn how to implement your organization’s governance plans. You learn how Azure policies can ensure operational decisions are enforced across the organization. You learn how to use resource tagging to improve reporting.

title: Lab 04 - Implement Virtual Networking
summary: This lab is the first of three labs that focuses on virtual networking. In this lab, you learn the basics of virtual networking and subnetting. You learn how to protect your network with network security groups and application security groups. You also learn about DNS zones and records.

title: Lab 05 - Implement Intersite Connectivity
summary: In this lab you explore communication between virtual networks. You implement virtual network peering and test connections. You will also create a custom route.

title: Lab 06 - Implement Network Traffic Management
summary: In this lab, you learn how to configure and test a public Load Balancer and an Application Gateway.

title: Lab 07 - Manage Azure Storage
summary: In this lab you learn to create storage accounts for Azure blobs and Azure files. You learn to configure and secure blob containers. You also learn to use Storage Browser to configure and secure Azure file shares.

title: Lab 08 - Manage Virtual Machines
summary: In this lab, you create and compare virtual machines to virtual machine scale sets. You learn how to create, configure and resize a single virtual machine. You learn how to create a virtual machine scale set and configure autoscaling.

title: Lab 09a - Implement Web Apps
summary: In this lab, you learn about Azure web apps. You learn to configure a web app to display a Hello World application in an external GitHub repository. You learn to create a staging slot and swap with the production slot. You also learn about autoscaling to accommodate demand changes.

title: Lab 09b - Implement Azure Container Instances
summary: In this lab, you learn how to implement and deploy Azure Container Instances.

title: Lab 09c - Implement Azure Container Apps
summary: In this lab, you learn how to implement and deploy Azure Container Apps.

title: Lab 10 - Implement Data Protection
summary: In this lab, you learn about backup and recovery of Azure virtual machines. You learn to create a Recovery Service vault and a backup policy for Azure virtual machines. You learn about disaster recovery with Azure Site Recovery.

title: Lab 11: Implement monitoring
summary: In this lab, you deploy a virtual machine with logs-based monitoring, verify that monitoring data is being collected, create an Activity Log alert and action group, suppress notifications during a maintenance period, and trigger the alert by deleting the virtual machine.

title: ConfigMaps

title: Secrets

title: Namespaces
summary: Namespaces provide a way to organize and isolate resources within a single Kubernetes cluster. Think on them as virtual clusters inside your physical cluster - they help you separate different applications, environments, or teams while sharing the same underlying infrastructure.

title: Pods
summary: Pods are the smallest deployable units in Kubernetes. A Pod represents one or more containers that share storage, network, and configuration settings for how they should run together.

title: Services
summary: Services provide stable network endpoints for accessing pods. Since pods are ephemeral and can be created/destroyed frequently, services give you consistent DNS names and IP addresses for reliable communication.

title: DaemonSets
summary: DaemonSets ensure that a copy of a pod runs on every node (or a subset of nodes) in your cluster. They are ideal for system-level services that must operate on all nodes, such as logging, monitoring, and network agents.

title: Deployments
summary: Deployments are the most common workload controller for running stateless applications. They make sure your application always runs the desired number of Pods - automatically handling creation, scaling, updates, and recovery.

title: workload management: StatefulSets
summary: StatefulSets manage applications that need stable identities and persistent storage . Unlike Deployments, where Pods are interchangeable, each Pod in a StatefulSet keeps a unique, predictable identity throughout its lifecycle.
